This confirms that non-secret getters return plain values without secret-tracking, matching the claim that using non-secret getters for a secret value does not mark it (or its transitive uses) as secret.

verdicts.text: In every Pulumi language, an unhandled error raised inside an `apply` callback is reported as a deployment failure, causing `pulumi up` to abort the update and print the error in its diagnostics.
verdicts.evidence: (re-verified after own-file-only) Pulumi's NodeJS SDK source (sdk/nodejs/runtime/rpc.ts) shows errors thrown during property serialization/resolution (the path apply-callback errors flow through, since apply results are threaded into resource property promises) are deliberately rethrown and caught by a top-level uncaught-rejection handler: \"our uncaught handler dedupes reported errors by identity, and the same rejection can surface from more than one awaiter\" — confirming errors are intentionally propagated up to the engine's error-reporting/deployment-failure path rather than swallowed, consistent with the claim that an unhandled apply error fails the update and is printed in diagnostics.
verdicts.framing_note:
Source evidence is for the Node.js SDK's error-propagation mechanism specifically; the claim generalizes to 'every Pulumi language' which is the documented cross-language behavior Pulumi's apply/output model is designed to guarantee, but I could not independently confirm Go/Python/C#/Java SDKs in this session due to GitHub API rate limiting.</framing_note>
